title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 55–58). Grothendieck is axiomatising the combinatorial-topological structure carried by a 'deployed' stratified space. The space of strata (or strata-germs) Σ = Σ*(0) carries an order relation (closure/incidence). Σ*(d) is the space of chains x_0 < … < x_d, and b : Σ*(d) → Σ is the target map (x_0<…<x_d) ↦ x_d. So the system {Σ*(d)} is the semi-simplicial nerve of the ordered space Σ, but it lives over Σ as a space. The previous page shows that the fibre of b over x is a finite totally ordered set. It also shows that the germs B_α at x, attached to the points z_α ∈ b^{-1}(x) ⊂ Σ*(1), are mutually transversal. Their intersections correspond to the points of Σ*(d) above x, as in a normal-crossings or corner structure.

This page.
- Margin: the tower … → Σ*(2) ⇉ Σ*(1) → Σ*(0), with maps s', b' and b.
- Main text: Σ'(1) is the space of strata of coniveau 1, with its associated map b : Σ'(1) → Σ_0 (a germ at x). Σ'(2) parametrises pairs of germs B, B' with {B} < {B'}.
- The question is how to recover the order relation on Σ itself from the relative order structure Σ*(1)/Σ*(0). The relative structure only gives a relatively totally ordered finite covering, and from it the whole semi-simplicial system. To get the order on Σ he adds a 'source' map (36) s = p_1 : Σ*(1) → Σ, subject to two conditions:
  - s is injective on each fibre b^{-1}(x), i.e. (s, b) : Σ*(1) → Σ × Σ is injective;
  - s(u) ≠ b(u), i.e. Im(s, b) ∩ diag = ∅ (strictness).
- He then begins (37)–(38): a map φ_2 : Σ*(2) → Σ*(1) ⊂ Σ × Σ, and a triple map Σ*(2) → Σ_0³. He crosses this out with the remark that there are no independent data pr_1, pr_2: once Σ*(1) embeds in Σ × Σ, the second face map is forced.
- The next page completes this. There is a unique p_2 : Σ*(2) → Σ*(1) with b∘p_2 = s∘b' and p_1∘p_2 = p_1∘s'. The square (Σ*(2), b', p_2; Σ*(1), s, b) must be cartesian, i.e. Σ*(2) = Σ*(1) ×_{s,Σ,b} Σ*(1): a Segal / composability condition. A transversality condition between s and the 'immersion tendante' b is the only non-algebraic condition. Finally x < y ⇔ ∃u, x = p_1 u, y = b u.

In modern terms: a poset internal to (stratified) spaces, presented as its semi-simplicial nerve. Source and target maps make Σ*(1) a relation (a subspace of Σ × Σ disjoint from the diagonal), and the Segal condition makes Σ*(2) the space of composable pairs. In addition, b is a finite 'immersion' with transversal branches, so that the whole system looks like the face structure of a manifold with corners / normal-crossings resolution. It serves the 'déploiement' programme: encode a stratified space with conical/cylindrical neighbourhoods by an unfolded object whose strata incidences are a space-valued poset.
errors: Minor counting inconsistency carried from the previous page. The chains ending at x of length d correspond to d-element subsets of Σ_{<x}. So with N(x) = card(Σ_{≤x}) the fibre should be P_d({1,…,N(x)−1}), or else N(x) should be card(Σ_{<x}).

The notation drifts between Σ'_(1), Σ*(1), Σ_0, Σ*(0) and Σ_1. The first attempt at (37)–(38), the map to Σ_0³, is abandoned because pr_1φ and pr_2φ are not independent data once (s, b) is injective. Grothendieck notices this himself in the margin.
No mathematical error in the stated equivalences. 'Injective on each fibre of b' ⇔ '(s, b) injective', and 'image avoids x' ⇔ 'Im(s, b) ∩ diagonal = ∅', are both correct.

ideas.what: Encoding the order on the space of strata by its semi-simplicial nerve Σ*(d) of chains, with target map b, and recovering the order from Σ*(1) ⊂ Σ × Σ via source/target maps
ideas.modern_name: internal poset/category in spaces presented by its nerve (semi-simplicial space)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ehresmann (internal categories); Grothendieck/Segal (nerve of internal categories, 1960s)
ideas.where_published: nerve of categories internal to a category in FGA (Techniques de descente / construction) and SGA 4; general background

ideas.what: Cartesian condition Σ*(2) = Σ*(1) ×_Σ Σ*(1) determining p_2 uniquely (next page)
ideas.usually_credited_to: G. Segal (1968, 1974); Rezk for complete Segal spaces

ideas.what: Fibres of b finite and totally ordered, with corresponding germs mutually transversal: b is an 'immersion tendante' whose multiple points are given by Σ*(d)
ideas.modern_name: semi-simplicial resolution of a normal-crossings / corner structure; face poset of a manifold with corners (⟨n⟩-manifolds)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge II simplicial resolutions); Jänich, Laures (⟨n⟩-manifolds); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (unzipping)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 sketches the 'dévissage' of stratified structures into manifolds with boundary/corners, without this formalism

ideas.what: Transversality between the source map s and the immersion b as the only non-algebraic axiom (next page)

missed.claim: The page treats the incidence order of strata not as a discrete poset but as a poset object in spaces, given by a Segal-type semi-simplicial space over Σ. The target map b is a transversal immersion, as in the corner structure of the deployed space. This anticipates the later description of stratified spaces by space-valued posets/exit data and by unzipping into manifolds with corners (Ayala–Francis–Tanaka, Lurie's exit-path formalism). The previously unpublished element is a concrete axiom set: s injective on b-fibres, avoiding the diagonal, a cartesian square, and one transversality condition.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Offers a minimal, essentially algebraic axiomatisation (plus one transversality condition) of the corner/incidence data of a resolved stratified space. It could be compared with the AFT unzipping construction and with Nand-Lal/Waas-type models of stratified homotopy theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The algebra on the page is a routine reconstruction of an internal poset from its nerve (source/target, Segal condition). The interest lies only in its use within Grothendieck's unpublished 'déploiement' programme. That programme foreshadows later work on unzipping stratified spaces into manifolds with corners, but this page itself contains no unexpected result.
transcription_corrections: Margin tower: Σ*(2) with arrows s', b' to Σ*(1), then b to Σ = Σ*(0). The middle term is written Σ*(1), with an overwritten Σ'.
'une germe en contact [?]' is more likely 'un germe en x', i.e. the germ at x attached to a stratum of coniveau 1.
'l'espace qui param[?] des germes B, B' ...' should read 'l'espace qui paramétrise des germes B, B' en x tels que {B} < {B'}'.
'la donnée d'une application bord [?]' is probably 'une application source' (consistent with s = p_1), preceded by 'il faut donner de plus' (not fully struck through).
In (36) the target is written 'Σ_0 = Σ*(0)'; the subscript was overwritten.
Margin note on the left reads roughly 'il n'y a pas de données pr1, pr2 indépendantes !' referring to the struck-out (37)–(38).
